system_overview: This specification models a parameterized reliable broadcast protocol with Byzantine faults, based on the one-round asynchronous reliable broadcast algorithm from Srikanth and Toueg's 1987 paper (Figure 7). The protocol allows correct processes to reliably deliver a broadcast message even when up to T out of N processes are Byzantine. Instead of modeling a dedicated broadcaster, the protocol uses initial values at each process to represent whether the broadcaster's INIT message was received.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes divided into two groups: correct processes and faulty (Byzantine) processes. The partition into correct and faulty sets is chosen nondeterministically at initialization, with exactly N-F correct processes and F faulty processes (where F is at most T). Correct processes follow the protocol; Byzantine processes may send arbitrary ECHO messages. The protocol requires N greater than 3T.
state_variables: The system tracks: the set of correct processes, the set of faulty processes, the control location of each process (indicating whether it received an INIT message, has not received one, has sent an ECHO, or has accepted), the set of messages received by each process (pairs of sender identity and message type), and the set of messages sent by all correct processes.
initial_state: Initially, no messages have been sent and no messages have been received. The set of correct processes has cardinality N-F, and faulty processes are the complement. Each process starts in one of two states: one indicating it received the broadcaster's INIT message, the other indicating it did not. A restricted initial state is also defined where no correct process received the INIT message (all start in the non-broadcast state).
actions: The protocol defines the following transitions: (1) A correct process may receive a set of new messages, which is a subset of all sent messages by correct processes combined with all possible messages from Byzantine processes. (2) If a correct process received the INIT message (starts in the broadcast-received state), it immediately accepts and sends an ECHO message to all. (3) If a correct process that has not yet sent ECHO receives at least N-2T ECHO messages from distinct senders but fewer than N-T, it sends ECHO to all but does not yet accept. (4) If a correct process that has not yet sent ECHO receives at least N-T ECHO messages from distinct senders, it sends ECHO and immediately accepts. (5) If a correct process that has already sent ECHO receives at least N-T ECHO messages from distinct senders, it accepts.
safety_properties: Unforgeability: if no correct process broadcasts (all start without the INIT message), then no correct process ever accepts. Type safety: program counters, message sets, and process sets remain within their defined domains throughout execution.
liveness_properties: Correctness: if all correct processes received the INIT message (all start in the broadcast state), then eventually all correct processes accept. Relay: if any correct process accepts, then eventually all correct processes accept.
model_bounds: For model checking: N=4, T=1, F=1. A second configuration for checking the no-broadcast case uses N=10, T=3, F=2. Messages consist only of ECHO type paired with sender identities.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the combined receive-and-act steps of correct processes, ensuring that if a correct process can forever receive messages from correct senders and act on them, it eventually does. The specification includes a variant without fairness for checking safety-only properties (unforgeability). The model requires N greater than 3T, T at least F, and F at least 0. The specification includes formal proof support for the unforgeability property.
